text: Could I see your badge, please?
I can read a technical drawing.
With this badge you can go into the tunnel.
Could you open the gate, please?
Could I have access to the north area?
My badge gives me access to every area at ground level.
I can sign the daily report, but I can't operate the machines.
I'm sorry, you're not allowed in the tunnel without training.
Could I have permission for the north area, please?
Could you sign this report, please?

Good morning, everyone. Ray Collins, with the rules for this week. Please listen, because the badges change on Monday. If you have a green badge, you are a visitor. You can walk on the yellow walkway with a guide, and that is all. You cannot go into the tunnel and you cannot operate anything. Blue badge: you have access to every area at ground level, and to the tunnel, if you have the training for confined spaces. Red badge: you can operate the machines, because you have the license for them. One more thing. Nobody signs a paper for another person. If you need permission for a new area, come and ask me, and I sign it myself. Thank you, and have a safe week.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. Good news from London: I finished the training last Friday, so I have the blue badge now. A year ago I was only a visitor here, and I waited at the gate with a green card in my hand. This week I can go down into the tunnel with my own crew, and I can sign the daily report. I still cannot operate the big machines. For that you need a license, and the course is six months long. Oh, and one favor: could you send me a photo of your badge? Ours are changing next month, and my supervisor wants to see how other sites do it. Thank you, and talk to you soon.

Giovanna arrives at the gate at seven o'clock. She shows her badge to the guard. The guard checks her training and opens the gate. She signs the book for the visitor from London. Then she asks: could you give him a green badge, please?
